title: Maintenance Planner Roadmap
summary: A Maintenance Planner coordinates maintenance activities, schedules inspections, allocates resources, tracks spare parts, prepares work packages and ensures maintenance tasks are planned in accordance with approved procedures and operational requirements.

facts.Current degree: Aviation & Aerospace Programmes (B.Sc Aviation / CPL Integrated / AME / BBA Aviation)

blocks.text: A Maintenance Planner coordinates maintenance activities, schedules inspections, allocates resources, tracks spare parts, prepares work packages and ensures maintenance tasks are planned in accordance with approved procedures and operational requirements.

In aerospace manufacturing and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO), the role supports aircraft, engines, components, tooling and production equipment. The exact responsibilities depend on whether the employer is an aircraft operator, MRO organization, aerospace manufacturer or component repair facility.

A Maintenance Planner is not necessarily an aircraft maintenance certifying engineer. Planning responsibilities and authority to inspect, approve or certify maintenance are separate, and regulated tasks must be performed by appropriately authorized personnel.

rows.text: Entry-level opportunities in maintenance planning, production planning, MRO coordination and maintenance records
Progression toward senior planning, material coordination, reliability planning or maintenance control
Potential movement into maintenance programme management, production control or maintenance planning leadership

blocks.text: Progression depends on technical experience, employer requirements, aviation approvals and demonstrated planning competence.

blocks.text: Year 3 — Aerospace MRO Systems and Reliability
Actual documentation, approvals and release procedures must follow the applicable regulatory framework and the organization's approved procedures.

items.text: FMEA for a sample maintenance process.
Inspection schedule and work-package planning exercise.

blocks.text: Year 4 — Advanced Planning and Production Control

blocks.label: Recommended final-year project
blocks.text: Develop an MRO Maintenance Planning and Control Dashboard.
The project should use simulated or authorized data. It must not be used to determine actual aircraft maintenance intervals or replace approved maintenance programmes.
A planner coordinates the work and monitors its progress. Technical inspections, maintenance decisions and certification remain the responsibility of appropriately authorized personnel.

blocks.label: Best portfolio project
blocks.text: Create an MRO planning dashboard that tracks planned work, labour hours, parts availability, maintenance backlog, schedule adherence and outstanding constraints. Include a documented workflow and clearly identify the data as simulated if real maintenance data is unavailable.

rows.text: Maintenance planning intern, production planning intern
MRO planning intern, maintenance records assistant, reliability intern
Maintenance Planning Trainee, Production Planning Trainee, MRO Operations Trainee

blocks.text: Seek opportunities with aircraft MRO organizations, airlines, aerospace manufacturers, component repair facilities and industrial maintenance departments.
Access to aircraft, technical records and maintenance environments may require background checks, safety training and employer authorization.

items.text: ERP and computerized maintenance management systems

blocks.text: For aerospace maintenance, study the applicable requirements and guidance from the relevant aviation authority. In India, this may include the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), depending on the activity and organization. International employers may work under frameworks such as EASA or FAA requirements.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: A general maintenance-planning course does not authorize someone to certify aircraft maintenance or perform regulated work. Required qualifications depend on the job, jurisdiction and organization.

items.text: PG Diploma in Aircraft Maintenance Management
PG Diploma in Quality or Reliability Engineering

blocks.text: An MBA can support management progression, while engineering postgraduate study may be more useful for technical planning, manufacturing or reliability specialization. The best choice depends on the intended role.
Career progression depends on employer structure, experience, technical competence and applicable qualifications.
AI and analytics can support forecasting, but maintenance intervals and regulated technical decisions must remain grounded in approved maintenance data and applicable procedures.

rows.text: Work packages, maintenance schedules, labour estimates
Work orders, technical records, maintenance task cards
Audit readiness, documentation control, non-conformance tracking
Resource allocation, cost control, stakeholder coordination
Approved maintenance data, safety and regulatory awareness

blocks.text: A strong graduate targeting Maintenance Planner roles should be able to:

items.text: Explain basic aircraft systems and MRO workflows.
Prepare maintenance schedules using provided task requirements.
Check parts, tools and documentation availability.
Track outstanding tasks and maintenance backlogs.
Use Excel to report maintenance performance.
Apply basic reliability and root-cause analysis methods.
Use or learn ERP, CMMS or MRO planning systems.
Coordinate with engineering, materials and maintenance teams.
Understand safety, quality and regulatory documentation requirements.
Identify scheduling constraints and propose practical improvements.
Respect the boundaries between planning responsibilities and authorized maintenance or certification decisions.

blocks.text: For Aviation & Aerospace Programmes – Aerospace Manufacturing / MRO → Maintenance Planner, the strongest positioning is:

“An aerospace maintenance-planning professional who combines engineering fundamentals, work-package scheduling, materials coordination, reliability analysis, technical documentation and safety-conscious resource management.”
